outcome.technical: plugins/audit/scripts/git/_worktrees.py: _reads_as now compares the file's raw bytes with `git cat-file --filters <commit>:<rel>` (smudge + EOL conversion under the tree's attributes and config) instead of `hash-object --no-filters`; docstring rewritten to state the comparison and its reason. The byte read needs undecoded stdout, so the subprocess call moved into a new _git_bytes(git_root, args, timeout) returning (code, bytes, stderr-text), and _git is now that answer with stdout decoded utf-8/replace exactly as before (same signature, same return shape, same (None, '', why) on no git). The rev-parse in _reads_as still goes through the injected runner; the content read goes to _git_bytes, said in the docstring. tests/test__worktrees.py: new _autocrlf_repo/_crlf_killed_move fixtures and _autocrlf_cases (un11 _reads_as under autocrlf: CRLF checkout True, LF-only False, foreign bytes False, and the on-disk CRLF asserted so the fixture cannot go vacuous; un12 restore_copy after a move killed part way through its checkout of the head - HEAD still at base, b.txt written CRLF - restores; un13 the next advance_task_tree finishes that move). un5's fixture now pins core.eol=lf: with `*.txt text` a checkout uses core.eol, native by default, which on windows is CRLF and would have turned un5 red there under the new comparison; its label reworded off the old mechanism. outcome.descriptive: A move killed part way through its checkout on a core.autocrlf=true (Git for Windows default) checkout no longer leaves a tree that no verb can settle: moved files are compared with what checkout writes, not with the raw blob.
